h1: The scoop schedule that logs your dog, your gate code, and the hours your yard sits empty

criteria.h1: The scoop schedule that logs your dog, your gate code, and the hours your yard sits empty
tableRows: Easy AppointmentsDocumented self-hosted appointment plugin marketed for service businesses (plugin version 4.0.3). WordPress admin screens cover locations, services, workers, an appointments list, a customer list, custom form fields, and CSV export. A window such as "scoop window, gate code, yard photo" is a booking you create; a service name such as dog waste removal or yard scooping is a label you configure. Neither is a documented default. Dog-name, gate-code, absence-window, yard-photo, property-address, owner-name, phone, email, or appointment-date questions are custom fields you add (textarea, select, input, checkbox, or file); they are not documented defaults. A booking is a calendar row, not proof of work - and a CSV export of "scoop window + gate code + yard photo" next to a named owner is still a calendar that answers when the crew is expected. Emails can include those custom fields and copy the appointment off-site. An optional GDPR setting can auto-remove customer data older than six months; that is not a default purge. Google Calendar, SMS, and payments are Pro. Google reCAPTCHA is optional. Public booking-form browser hosts are unverified. | Dog-waste-removal service bookings stored on your WordPress site | Browser hosts not verified | Not assessed | Not tested | None | WordPress.org listingv4.0.3 readme.txt (SVN)

Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form BuilderDocumented self-hosted form builder (plugin version 1.58.1). The listing states Forminator stores and organizes submissions so you can sort, analyze, and manage responses, and includes a free file-upload field with multi-file support. Version 1.58.1 helper-fields.php forminator_upload_root() writes under the WordPress uploads directory plus /forminator/, with per-form hashed subfolders from forminator_get_upload_path(). upload.php stores files through that path. Dog-name, gate-code, absence-window, yard-photo, property-address, owner-name, phone, email, or appointment-date questions are fields you add; they are not documented defaults. Optional yard photo uploads are files you accept; that file type is not a documented default. A yard photo is a stored file, not a map of the property. A gate-code note is stored text, not a key to the house. A dog-waste-removal form is not proof anyone entered the yard. Notification emails can copy field values and file links off-site. Optional Stripe, PayPal, HubSpot, Mailchimp, and webhook integrations send data only when you enable them. Public form-page browser hosts are unverified. How long a yard photo sits after a visit that never happened is not a documented default of the plugin. | Gate-code and absence-window answers stored in WordPress; optional yard-photo uploads in the site uploads/forminator folder | Browser hosts not verified | Not assessed | Not tested | None | WordPress.org listingv1.58.1 readme.txt (SVN)v1.58.1 helper-fields.php (upload root)v1.58.1 upload.php

Iptanus File UploadDocumented frontend upload form (formerly WordPress File Upload). By default files land inside the wp-content directory of the site; the upload path is configurable. Uploaded files can be added to Media or attached to the current page. FTP and SFTP destinations are documented. The Professional version documents uploads to Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, or Amazon S3. A yard photo or route-sheet PDF is a file you accept; that file type is not a documented default. An uploaded yard photo is a stored file, not a map of the property. Deleting a form entry later does not by itself prove the file was removed from the uploads path or from a cloud destination you enabled. The listing claims GDPR compliance without a tested EXIF-strip or retention length here. Review upload directory, Media attachment, and cloud destinations. Browser hosts for the visitor upload path were not verified for this snapshot. Iptanus File UploadDocumented frontend upload form (formerly WordPress File Upload). By default files land inside the wp-content directory of the site; the upload path is configurable. Uploaded files can be added to Media or attached to the current page. FTP and SFTP destinations are documented. The Professional version documents uploads to Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, or Amazon S3. A wall photo or mount-spec PDF is a file you accept; that file type is not a documented default. An uploaded wall photo is a stored file, not an inventory of electronics. Deleting a form entry later does not by itself prove the file was removed from the uploads path or from a cloud destination you enabled.
